# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three wires. Position 1 is smooth. Position 2 has a small ridge near the base. Position 3 is textured like sandpaper.
Deaf says to Mute: DISPLAY 0 LIGHT YELLOW WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW

I hold the manual. The rule is unambiguous: count the blue flashes only while the light is lit; once it goes dark the flashing is over, and that final count picks the wire — 0→red, 1→green, 2→red, 3→green, 4→red, 5→green.

The Deaf monkey can see but cannot hear me, so my gestures are what they receive. They just reported "DISPLAY 0" alongside a yellow light and green/red/yellow wires. That reads as the current state of the display and lamp, not necessarily the completed flash count — I have no confirmation yet that the light has gone dark, which is when the flashing is officially over. So before I relay any cut decision, I need to know whether the blue flashing has finished and what the total was.

The Blind monkey gave tactile positions (smooth / ridge / sandpaper) but cannot see colour, so they cannot map a position to red or green on their own; the colour must come from the Deaf monkey's eyes. Right now I do not even know if there is a blue wire among them, nor how many times the light flashed blue.

Therefore my first move is to ask the Deaf monkey to watch for the light going dark and then show me the number of blue flashes using fingers. I gesture: point at the light, then hold up fingers meaning "how many," with an open palm meaning "wait/hold." This prompts them to report the count once the flashing ends.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "✋", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: State: Display 0, Light Yellow. Wires: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Yellow. What action?
Deaf says to Mute: LIGHT CHANGED TO BLUE DISPLAY STILL 0 WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW

I hold the manual. The rule: count blue flashes only while the light is lit; once it goes dark the flashing is over, and that final count picks the wire (0→red, 1→green, 2→red, 3→green, 4→red, 5→green).

What I just learned from Deaf: the light has changed to BLUE and the display still reads 0. So the blue flashing sequence has begun (or is ongoing) and is not yet finished — the display counter is still at 0. That means the cut decision is premature: I must wait until the light goes dark and the display shows its final number before relaying any wire colour. If I acted now on "display 0" I would be guessing that zero flashes occurred, which contradicts a light that is currently blue.

Blind cannot see colours, so they need the final colour relayed through Deaf's eyes. Right now there is nothing actionable for Blind except to hold. My job this turn is to tell Deaf, by gesture, to keep watching and report the final display number once the light goes dark, and to tell Blind to wait.

For Deaf I gesture: point down at the light (👇), then open hand meaning stop/wait (✋), then thumbs up meaning good/keep going (👍), then pointing finger meaning watch/report (👆). This asks them to continue observing until darkness and then show me the final count with fingers. For Blind I gesture a clear "wait": open hand (✋).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "✋", "👍", "👆"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: State: Disp 0, Light Blue, Wires 1-Green 2-Red 3-Yellow. Indicate wire to cut.

I hold the manual. The rule is explicit: count blue flashes only while the light is lit; once it goes dark the flashing is over, and that final count picks the wire (0→red, 1→green, 2→red, 3→green, 4→red, 5→green).

Blind is asking me to indicate a wire now. But the latest state I have — from Deaf last round and echoed by Blind — is Light BLUE with Display still 0. A blue light means the flashing sequence is in progress, not finished. If I told them to cut on "display 0" right now, I would be treating an ongoing flash as zero, which is exactly the trap the manual warns about ("when the light goes dark, the flashing is over"). Cutting early could detonate the bomb. So I must refuse to give a cut decision until the light goes dark and the display shows its final number.

Also note: I cannot see the bomb or touch it, so even when the count is known, the colour-to-position mapping must come through Deaf's eyes to Blind. Right now there is no safe action except to wait for the end of flashing.

To Deaf (who can see my gestures), I signal clearly: stop / do not act yet (👎), then point at the light (👇) meaning watch it, then open hand (✋) meaning wait until it goes dark. This asks them to keep observing and report the final display value only after darkness. To Blind, who cannot see gestures, I cannot convey anything visual; but Blind's message reached me via text, and they need to know to hold. Since I cannot speak and gestures are invisible to them, the only channel to Blind is... none directly. Therefore I rely on Deaf to relay "wait" to Blind once they understand my gesture, or simply ensure no cut happens. My actionable output is the gesture to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👇", "✋"])
```
